key_insight: RASP separates reading from learning: inference uses all LoRA atoms, while training updates only a sparse subset within one fixed-size adapter.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support memory-bounded continual adaptation of engineering vision systems, but the abstract reports no solid-mechanics or constitutive-modeling validation.
method: A scene-modulated cosine router selects the top-q unlocked atoms for gradient updates while inference retains all r atoms.
A Frobenius Gram-coherence penalty separates active output directions from non-updated directions.
Router activation histories and atom spectral norms guide Cauchy step attenuation and boundary anchor locking.
evidence_signal: Across CIFAR-100, CUB-200, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-A, the abstract reports matching or surpassing branch-expanding LoRA learners with a strictly constant parameter footprint.
watch_item: Long-horizon capacity under progressive atom locking remains unclear; the abstract provides no quantitative saturation analysis.
paper_title: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA
